title: Berg v Berg, 2011 NY Slip Op 05440
summary: Official New York appellate opinion rejecting alleged Beth Din misconduct/partiality while vacating an attorney-fee portion of the award for lack of contractual authorization.

evidence.claim: The Second Department held that the appellant did not establish prejudicial arbitrator misconduct or disqualifying partiality, but vacated the award's attorney-fee and future-legal-expense provisions because the arbitration agreement did not expressly authorize attorneys' fees.

caveats: The opinion does not identify a stable institutional name for the Beth Din, so no organization identity is inferred from this case.

summary: Kings County Article 75 review of a Beth Din Bais Hora'ah Etz Chaim award; asserted misconduct grounds were rejected and the award was confirmed except for an unauthorized attorney-fee provision.

evidence.claim: The court denied the cross-petition to vacate, found no established prejudicial arbitral misconduct on the asserted grounds, and confirmed the award except for a legal-expense provision that exceeded the authority conferred by the arbitration agreement.

counterevidence: The court rejected the respondent's asserted misconduct/evidentiary/cross-examination grounds on the record before it.
caveats: Limited modification of an attorney-fee remedy is classified as excess of arbitral authority, not corruption.

title: Berg v Berg
summary: Second Department review of a Beth Din award; alleged misconduct/partiality was not established, while attorney-fee provisions were vacated for lack of authorization in the arbitration agreement.

evidence.claim: The appellate court rejected asserted prejudicial misconduct and partiality grounds, but modified the lower-court order to vacate the attorney-fee and future-legal-expense portions of the Beth Din award because the arbitration agreement did not provide for attorneys' fees.

counterevidence: The appellant did not establish that alleged arbitrator impropriety or misconduct prejudiced his rights or the integrity of the arbitration.
caveats: The opinion does not provide a stable tribunal name; no institution identity is inferred.
Partial vacatur of a remedy is not classified as corruption.

title: Beth Din civil-review classification — pass 2
summary: Classification of two official New York opinions to preserve rejected misconduct allegations, limited remedy modification, exact tribunal identity, and counterevidence without converting ordinary arbitration review into corruption findings.

caveats: These cases expand the civil-review ledger but do not complete the cross-jurisdiction corpus.

data.question: How should Schwimmer v Malinas and Berg v Berg be represented in the Beth Din misconduct/civil-review corpus without overstating routine arbitration review?
data.method: Review official New York opinions, resolve exact tribunal identity only where the record names it, separate allegations from adjudicated holdings, and classify remedy modification separately from misconduct findings.
data.framework: allegation → court review → adjudicated disposition → remedy modification → institution identity
data.scope: New York civil review of Beth Din arbitration awards; bounded pass 2 for issue #2646
findings: Schwimmer identifies Beth Din Bais Hora'ah Etz Chaim and rejects the asserted misconduct/vacatur grounds, while refusing to confirm an unauthorized attorney-fee provision.
Berg rejects asserted prejudicial misconduct/partiality and separately vacates unauthorized attorney-fee/future-expense provisions.
Neither decision supports labeling the tribunal or arbitrators corrupt; both are valuable counterevidence and procedural-disposition records.
conclusions: The corpus should represent misconduct allegations, rejected allegations, and excess-of-authority remedy corrections as distinct states.
Exact tribunal identity may be created for Schwimmer, while Berg remains institution-unresolved because the appellate opinion does not name a stable tribunal.
limitations: This pass does not retrieve every lower-court filing, arbitration record, or tribunal governance document.
It covers only two New York civil-review decisions.
